# Norway Land and Property



[Norway](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Norway_Genealogy "Norway Genealogy")

Land and Property

## Resources

### Online Resources

* **1886** [Norway, Cadastres, 1886](https://www.myheritage.com/research/collection-20196/norway-cadastres-1886) at MyHeritage — index ($)
* [Opplysninger om eiendom (Information about Real Estate Registers)](https://www.arkivverket.no/opplysninger-om-eiendom)
* [Norway Land Records Online](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Norway_Land_Records_Online "Norway Land Records Online")

### Offices to Contact

## Background

Land records generally start in the 1700s. These records contain information about [real estate conveyances, mortgages](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Norway:Deeds "Norway:Deeds"), [contracts](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Norway_Cottager_Contracts "Norway Cottager Contracts"), agreements, deeds, leases of land, and auction sales [Pension contracts](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Norway:_Pension_Contracts "Norway: Pension Contracts") show the inheritance of property from one generation to the next. Land records often reveal family information, such as the name of a spouse, heir, and other relatives. From land records you may learn where people lived previously, their occupations, and other clues for further research. Sometimes you will find information about entire families.

For the period before 1700, you may wish to search [Norway Court Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Norway_Court_Records "Norway Court Records"). They contain similar property information.

The land records after 1865 are in the custody of the local magistrate (*sorenskriver*). They are also available up to 1935 at the regional archives, but only in book form. The records before 1865 are in the custody of the regional archives and are available on microfilm at the FamilySearch Library.

See [Norway Taxation](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Norway_Taxation "Norway Taxation") for information on land and tax divisions.

### Types of Records

* Example cottager contract: [Norway Cottager Contracts](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Norway_Cottager_Contracts "Norway Cottager Contracts")
* Example retirement contract: [Norway Retirement Contracts](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Norway_Retirement_Contracts "Norway Retirement Contracts")

#### Land Records (*Fast Eiendomsprotokoller*)

These records contain useful lineage linking information, can be used to establish relationships. Most are not indexed. They include records of land ownership and land taxation. Among these are revenue district accounts (*Fogedregnskaber*), rural district accounts (*Lensregnkaper*), urban district accounts (*Byregnskaper*), land books (*Jordebøker*), and land commissions (*Landkommisjoner*). Most records date from about 1600.
The following information may be found in these records:

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **Land books**   * Land rentals * Names, dates, land quantities | **Property taxation**   * Tax lists * Real estate registers of owners and cultivators of farms * Quantities of land and monetary amounts * Heads of taxed households * Possibly other family members |

* See [Norway Matrikkel](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Norway_Matrikkel "Norway Matrikkel") for more information.

#### Mortgage Books (*Pantebøker*)

These records contain useful lineage linking information, can be used to establish relationships. In many cases the mortgage books can be used as a substitute index to the probate records. The information from the mortgage records can extend pedigree lines as much as three generations. Most are not indexed and begin in the 1700s.

The following information may be found in these records:

* Information regarding real estate conveyances, mortgages and other encumbrances
* Agreements, deeds, contracts
* Date of the document
